title: Decision & Economic Mapping for Model Supply Chain
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: create a reproducible decision framework and economic model that maps competitor model availability, performance, and pricing to Redwood product-level procurement and fallback rules. This will let PM and GTM teams quantify trade-offs (latency, cost, quality) and trigger procurement actions or rollout changes automatically. Scope: market scan of 6 candidate model sources (open and hosted), a pricing elasticity model for token/throughput impacts, and a decision matrix for fallback sequencing used by the routing policy team.
updates: 2026-02-10: Kickoff completed with Research, Eng (runtime), and Finance. Agreed on scope: 6 suppliers, 3 workload archetypes (RAG low-latency, chat medium-latency, embeddings high-throughput).

2026-02-18: Completed baseline telemetry spec — what we need from telemetry pipeline (p95 latency per model, token-cost, error rates, estimated token equivalence between model families). Eng owner for telemetry: Jonah Reed.

2026-02-27: Compiled preliminary pricing snapshots for models A-F using public docs and direct vendor quotes. Early signal: model C offers 40% lower per-token but has 2x p95 latency for short-context chat.

2026-03-03: Running synthetic workload probes in field-lab (3 tenants). First-run results show expected latency/cost trade-offs; quality delta measured with 200 prompts from our eval set shows Model E maintains quality on RAG queries better than quantized variants.

2026-03-09: Review with Finance — introduced a 'break-even per-request threshold' where switching to cheaper model increases developer cost due to retries and latency SLO violations. Finance proposed a 25% cushion for SLA-bound customers.
2026-03-12: Draft decision engine spec completed. Next: engineering spike to prototype rule enforcement in routing layer and a PM review to finalize procurement triggers.
review_comments: Jonah Reed (ENG): Suggest adding probe coverage for cold KV cache warmup; latency delta in first 10 tokens is a major driver for perceived UX.
Liam Chen (Finance): We need model-level minimum commitment assumptions — vendor minimums will change economic calculation for Dedicated customers.
Talia Park (Design): If fallback adds >150ms we should show a UX treatment in Console explaining degraded mode and expected ETA to recover.
Product Leadership: Prefer rule transparency — expose to teams why a fallback occurred (model, rationale, compensated cost).
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix completed and reviewed by Eng/Finance/Legal
Prototype routing rule created that can be toggled per-customer and logs rationale
Cost model validated against synthetic workload and aligned with Finance assumptions
Dashboard tile in Console showing real-time supply-risk index and recommended fallback sequence
success_metrics: Reduction in SLA breaches caused by model supply outages by 60% in first quarter after rollout
Improved median cost-per-inference by 8% for non-SLA customers while maintaining quality metrics
Time-to-fallback from outage detection to active fallback policy < 30s in 95% of incidents
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Vendor pricing or T&Cs change post-procurement. Mitigation: contract clauses + 30-day re-eval triggers.
Risk: Quality regressions on cheaper models. Mitigation: automatic canary traffic with quality regressors; manual escalation to PM.
Risk: Telemetry blind spots (e.g., cross-region variance). Mitigation: required labeling of probes by region and workload archetype.
research_plan: 1) Market telemetry harvest: scrape public pricing and benchmark docs for 6 candidate models; request vendor test accounts where possible.
2) Field-lab probes: run 3 synthetic workloads for 48h with KV-cache warmups and multi-context lengths.
3) Quality delta analysis: run 2k evaluation prompts per model, compute pass/fail on our prompt-based rubric and human-verified subset.
4) Economic sensitivity: vary throughput and latency SLO thresholds to compute break-even points per customer archetype.

notes: We intentionally separate 'procurement triggers' from 'routing rules' to allow procurement cadence to lag by one cycle without breaking runtime fallback behavior.
Consider adding a weekly 'supply risk' digest for sales and customer success when a model crosses the break-even threshold for a top-50 customer.
Prototype should be designed for both hosted API customers and Dedicated pools; fallback ordering may differ by customer tier.
